what_its_for: Avapritinib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with certain types of stomach and intestinal tumors called gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) that have a specific gene change (mutation) in a gene called PDGFRA. It is also used to treat a rare condition called advanced systemic mastocytosis, which is a disease where too many abnormal mast cells build up in the body.
how_to_take: Take avapritinib by mouth (swallow the tablet whole). You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablet. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose as usual.
dosing: For GIST tumors: The usual dose is 300 mg taken once daily. For systemic mastocytosis: The usual dose is 200 mg taken once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or stop your treatment temporarily if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your health and other medications you take.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 8 hours away. If your next dose is within 8 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store avapritinib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Store it away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel confused, dizzy, or have memory problems, as this drug can affect your thinking and coordination. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements, because many medicines can interact with avapritinib. Avoid strong antifungal medications (like ketoconazole) and certain antibiotics unless your doctor approves them. Do not become pregnant while taking this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: confusion, memory loss, difficulty speaking or finding words, dizziness, or changes in personality or behavior (these may be signs of a serious brain side effect called intracranial hemorrhage or cognitive effects); unusual bruising or bleeding; severe headache; vision changes; shortness of breath or swelling in your legs or arms; signs of infection such as fever or chills; nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is severe or does not go away; or if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant, or plan to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Some patients may begin to see benefits within the first few weeks of treatment, but it may take several months to see the full effect. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups, blood tests, and imaging scans. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own even if you feel well — stopping without your doctor's guidance could allow the disease to come back or get worse.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 weeks after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for at least 6 weeks after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially those affecting the brain such as confusion or memory problems. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
